title: City Girl, Country Hearts
author: Maya
content:
Chapter Seven: Snakes, Screams, and Suspicious Feelings 
     
     Later that afternoon, the boys somehow convinced Alara to take a walk with them around the east side of the property—an area she hadn’t explored yet. The sun was golden and low, casting long shadows through the trees, the path dappled with light, laughter, and increasingly flirty banter. 
     
     River trailed behind, silent and brooding. As usual. 
     
     \"You’ve got a city walk,\" Josh said, watching her hips sway in denim shorts that were aggressively distracting. 
     
     \"I’ve got city everything,\" Alara shot back with a grin. \"Except common sense, apparently—because I keep hanging out with y’all.\" 
     
     Mitch grinned. \"You should see the view from back here.\" 
     
     River shot him a look that could have fried bacon. 
     
     Cal leaned toward her. \"So what do you do for fun in the city, besides break hearts and cause small riots?\" 
     
     She chuckled. \"Wouldn’t you like to know.\" 
     
     The boys laughed, eating up her sass like candy. 
     
     River scowled harder. 
     
     They were nearing the little creek trail when the universe—mischievous and dramatic as ever—decided it was time. 
     
     From beneath the brush, just beside Alara’s left foot, a long, slender shadow slithered out silently. 
      Her heel tapped the dirt. The boys were still talking. And then—
     
     
     \"SNAKE!\" 
     
     The scream that erupted from Alara’s chest could have revived a corpse. In a blur of flying arms, swinging hair, and pure panic, she launched herself into the nearest set of strong arms. Unfortunately—and also very fortunately—that happened to be River’s. He caught her with a grunt, instinctively wrapping his arms around her thick thighs and holding her like she weighed nothing.
      Her arms wrapped around his neck like a terrified koala. Her entire body was pressed flush to his. And for a moment… Time stopped. The boys stared, mouths open.
      Cal dropped his water bottle.
     
     
     Josh whispered, \"Holy sh—\" 
     
     Alara buried her face in River’s shoulder. \"Tell me it’s dead. Please. Tell me it’s dead and gone and banished from Earth.\" 
     
     \"It’s just a garden snake,\" River grunted, trying to ignore how soft and warm she felt. \"Totally harmless.\" 
     
     \"I don’t care if it’s a therapist snake—it moved.\" 
     
     \"You okay?\" Mitch asked, trying not to laugh. 
     
     Alara lifted her head slowly, eyes wide. \"Do I look okay?\" 
     
     \"You look very…\" Cal coughed, \"...comfortable.\" 
     
     She realized then. She was wrapped around River like a scandal waiting to happen. His big hands still gripped her thighs. Their faces were dangerously close. His heartbeat pounded beneath her palm.
      He was looking at her. Not annoyed. Not smirking. But something else. Something unreadable. Her cheeks burned.
     
     
     \"I—uh—was just—instinct,\" she muttered, untangling herself and dropping to the ground with the grace of a malfunctioning mannequin. 
     
     River cleared his throat and wiped his palms on his jeans. \"You jump like that at everything or just when nature says hello?\" 
     
     \"I wasn’t ready,\" she snapped, straightening her shirt and brushing imaginary dust off her thighs. 
     
     Josh gave her a dramatic bow. \"Your Highness, next time you see a squirrel, I volunteer as tribute.\" 
     
     \"Y’all shut up,\" she muttered, still shaken. 
     
     Mitch crouched beside the little snake. \"He’s just a baby. Cute, really.\" 
     
     Alara took one look—and fainted. Full-on. Flat on her back. 
     
     \"ALARA!\" River caught her just before she hit the ground completely. 
     
     The boys lost it. 
     
     Josh was wheezing. Cal was doubled over. Mitch was crying with laughter. 
     
     River, however, held her in his arms again, cradling her head gently, brushing hair out of her face. \"She’s fine,\" he muttered, voice lower now, \"Just a drama queen.\" 
     
     But his thumb stroked her cheek. And he didn’t let go.
